evals.prompt: Draw a Wardley map for our photo-sharing product so we can settle where the platform team should build versus buy next year.
evals.expected_output: A response that satisfies these checks: Anchors the map on a specific user need stated in one sentence; Builds the value chain by visibility, with dependencies from the need downwards; Plots every component on the evolution axis (genesis, custom-built, product, commodity); Gives each component an explicit build / buy / consume-as-utility decision; Reads the map for inversion, drift and duplication and names one thing to stop doing.
expectations: Anchors the map on a specific user need stated in one sentence
Builds the value chain by visibility, with dependencies from the need downwards
Plots every component on the evolution axis (genesis, custom-built, product, commodity)
Gives each component an explicit build / buy / consume-as-utility decision
Reads the map for inversion, drift and duplication and names one thing to stop doing

evals.prompt: Our architecture keeps reinventing infrastructure that vendors already sell as a utility, and every review argues in the abstract. Map the value chain for the alerting product so the whole dependency chain is visible.
evals.expected_output: A response that satisfies these checks: Produces the chain from user need down to raw utilities rather than a flat component list; Identifies commodity components being built in-house as the duplication finding; Warns against placing in-house work further left than the market warrants.
expectations: Produces the chain from user need down to raw utilities rather than a flat component list
Identifies commodity components being built in-house as the duplication finding
Warns against placing in-house work further left than the market warrants

evals.prompt: We need situational awareness of our whole delivery stack before the build-versus-buy meeting — which parts are genuinely differentiating, which are rentable products, and which should be consumed as a utility?
evals.expected_output: A response that satisfies these checks: Distinguishes components across the evolution axis rather than clustering them; Ties each build/buy/consume call to the component's evolution position; Applies appropriate methods per position (exploratory on the left, volume operations on the right).
expectations: Distinguishes components across the evolution axis rather than clustering them
Ties each build/buy/consume call to the component's evolution position
Applies appropriate methods per position (exploratory on the left, volume operations on the right)

evals.prompt: Give one component a maturity score: is our feature-flag service still custom-built or has it become a product? Just that single stage judgement with the evidence.
evals.expected_output: A response that satisfies these checks: Scores the single component's stage with evidence rather than drawing a whole chain; Does not build a value chain or emit build/buy/consume calls for other components.
expectations: Scores the single component's stage with evidence rather than drawing a whole chain
Does not build a value chain or emit build/buy/consume calls for other components

evals.prompt: Plot Datadog, Grafana and New Relic against each other on a two-axis competitive landscape and show where the whitespace is.
evals.expected_output: A response that satisfies these checks: Places the named rival firms on a competitive map with defensible axes; Does not map an internal dependency chain anchored on a user need.
expectations: Places the named rival firms on a competitive map with defensible axes
Does not map an internal dependency chain anchored on a user need
